pages.title: Glueball Core
pages.text: Gluons carry the very colour charge they mediate, so in principle they can bind to one another with no quarks at all. This is that bound state: a knot of pure strong force, heavy and warm, with nothing inside it but the glue. Lattice QCD predicted it for decades; I am holding one.

$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)I stripped the quarks out of a quark-gluon plasma beam using strange matter as a sink and a qubit to tag what remained. Most runs left nothing. One left a dense, colourless sphere of self-interacting gluons that refused to decay.
